outcomes.text: Keepers are paid by the in-library V1 formula for verified work (R95): (min(measured gas, operation gas bound, maxGas) + overhead) x min(transaction gas price, basefee + priority allowance, gas price ceiling) + the work fee per processed draw, reconciled draw and listed Shape unit, limited by real operating liquidity and the pool's 0.622 ETH / floor(0.05 ETH per 12 seconds) spending bucket. There is no separate absolute payment ceiling. Caller minimum is atomic. Initial economics: 60k overhead gas and 0.00002 ETH work fee. In the explicitly named reference regimes, the measured compensation above billed gas, after subtracting the stated gas-overhead and service allowances, is at most 100,000 gas per draw (owner approval 2026-11-23, was 80,000: paid processing of stuck draws after the grace keeps FWA's storage refunds). This is the retained-refund metric, not total EVM refunds or a universal immutable refund cap. Independent processing-only measurements are reported with that narrower scope.

Restocking surcharges are included in Shape/Pack listing prices and realized indirectly through successful purchases, not collected on listing. Creators front actual minting and operating expenses. In the explicitly named V1 reference regimes, expected surcharge contribution still listed is at most 0.2613 ETH (55 contained Shape units x 0.00475 ETH at the 5 gwei cap with 910k restock gas imply 0.26125 ETH; owner approval 2026-11-23, was 0.26 ETH). This scenario check is neither liquid cash nor capital locked upfront, and is not a limit for larger boards or other economics.

Closing releases missing inventory, setup and working-buffer requirements. While paid upkeep is enabled, only actual unreconciled draws times their current immutable reconciliation budget are retained. Disabling paid upkeep releases that hold; re-enabling is immediate and needs the maintenance budget funded. Buyer refunds and FWA edge remain in FWA. Completed paid work receives its atomic formula payment; future work is not a keeper debt.
Exact redeemable backing: every prize unlisted redeems for exactly its backing.

Under the capital-efficient continuity guarantee, Add ETH or Continue without a missing top prize supports ongoing operation in the named response regimes: they finish with admission open. Later adverse wins may again leave target prizes missing; days of depletion and capital shortfalls remain reported. This supersedes the old immediate/full-target-restoration promise, not backing or purchaser refund rights.

Closeout returns everything: after the closeout the Balancer, its listed backing and its FWA proceeds hold nothing. Exception, under FWA's rules: an NFT whose delivery failed stays at FWA until its winner takes the refund.

Ordinary funded launch-board operation admits reconciled purchases under the existing70% weight/busy gate, plus the curated gate only in curated-required mode. A Shapes mint fee above the accepted cap stops restocking, not purchases of listed prizes. Adverse low-capital depletion may pause and requires existing proceeds, Add ETH, a smaller target or closing; no automatic refill from refused demand is promised. The named ordinary regimes have zero low-inventory refusals within the5gwei V1 cap.

Actual collected FWA owner proceeds create floor(amount × stored creatorRevenueBps / 10,000) credit exactly once. Capital returns create none. Paid and unpaid work protect existing credit; claims remain available during inventory depletion. Historical markup attribution and its drift threshold are superseded; previous signatures do not approve this changed outcome.

On the launch board at steady normal gas (basefee 0.1 gwei), a player pays at most 1.5x the expected Shape backing of a draw: FWA's all-in quote (draw price and randomness fee) against the backing weighted as FWA weighs draws, checked before every draw (R19, D17). After a gas spike, prices stay higher until the prizes listed during it are won again (1.71x after 60 draws restocked at 5 gwei); a creator's own markup and NFT values can exceed it (2.27x at 100% markup): shown as information.

In the explicitly named fixed-input launch-board regressions, the request-board surcharge component of realized FWA owner proceeds covers play keeper payouts over 180 draws, excluding creator setup. This zero-shortfall check is not a guarantee for every gas transition, purchase ordering, liquidity path or board. An independent 60-low/60-high/60-low gas path with 5 ETH opening capital has a 0.018420439573763843 ETH surcharge-only shortfall; the minimum-opening comparison has a different inventory/cash path and a 0.000996429671423091 ETH surplus. Neither implies a demand forecast or universal net creator profit. Historical NFT-dominated shortfalls of about 0.038 ETH describe named examples, not a maximum.

In the named quiet launch-board regimes the creator ends ahead after180draws, counting claimed/currentassets againstdeposits/contributions at0.1,0.5,2and5gwei. Adverse large-prize outcomes andzero-demandcosts areinformation. The current large_win regime forces one real0.5ETHwin without assuming it can immediatelybe replaced forasecondwin; historicaltwo-wincomparisonis superseded.

(D16) Draws settle with only players, the randomness service and keepers acting, while the factory's keeper list is open or names an active keeper: upkeep processes FWA's queue, so no day ends with a draw unsettled, including draws that reserved a staged restock and lost FWA's randomness fast path, and bursts that leave five draws waiting at once (the tested burst size; FWA checks the operator once per batch and actual outstanding counts can exceed five; keepers process two per call). In curated-required mode sales keep going only while a curated NFT is listed: the regimes relist each won NFT as the creator would; after the last is won, sales pause until the creator lists another. In standard mode a pool keeps selling Shapes with no curated NFT listed (shapes_only, mixed_to_shapes_only).

An immediate local economics change with outstanding draws (R95: there is no policy to replace) changes only the pool's economics, preserves all existing listing prices, needs operating funding only when the maintenance exposure grows, and reconciles through closeout without moving assets to another pool.

At basefee0.5gwei, mintfee0.001ETH and V1 enabled, twenty small Shapes actually open and finish paid setup with exactly 0.229565 ETH initial pool funding (one fee schedule: 3.2M gas, 60k overhead gas, 0.00002 ETH work fee; owner approval 2026-11-23, was 0.2356 ETH), then ordinary operation runs without creator ETH top-ups. Purchaser backing/refunds remain separately protected. This is the reached board/context, not a universal deposit or income guarantee.

The minimum-capital operating regimes add zero creator ETH after opening; depleted inventory and refusal/recovery statistics remain visible rather than hidden by automatic deposits. Curated NFT relisting, where performed, is separately counted.
